text:
Maria Chen: Heads up — canary rolling of r/4578 (kernel-router + batching heuristics) is triggering OOMs on long prompts (>= 40k tokens). Seen on 3 nodes so far, all p4d-large. Needs triage, looks rollout-blocker.
infra-bot: deploy r/4578 -> canary started (canary=5%) :rocket:
Samir Patel: logging? stack traces?
Maria Chen: paste logs: `oom: failed to allocate 256MB slab for kv-cache:pagelet_alloc failed (errno=12)`
Maria Chen: also pmap snapshot: `kv_slab: resident=6.1G, anon=2.3G, fragmented=1.9G (estimated)`
Zhang Wei: CI perf test also flagged a +18% tail latency regression on longctx benchmark after that merge (regression window matches r/4578).
Devon O'Neill: my suspicion: kernel selection change now prefers fast-attn kernel for mid-length batches; combined with new batching boundary logic, we're causing more small allocations and preventing compaction. Slab rebalancer seems starved.
Samir Patel: doing quick bisect locally. If it's r/4578 I'll try toggle kernel-policy to previous.
Samir Patel: bisect result: reprod on commit 1a2b3c4 -> lands a change in runtime/kernel_router.cc: prefer_fast_path_for_seq >= 256.
Samir Patel: diff snippet: `if (seq_len >= 256) choose(FastAttn); else choose(Generic);` (previously threshold was 1024)
Maria Chen: that explains sequence-length sensitivity — long prompts with mixed segments get broken into mid-seq batches and hit the fast-attn path which allocs transient KV pagelets and prevents coalescing.
Devon O'Neill: reproducer: run longctx with mixed-short-prefixes (see `tests/longctx/regen_long_prompt.sh`) and watch kv slab allocations: `./tools/kv_monitor --hist --freq=200ms` shows repeated 128MB allocations then failures.
ops: recommend pausing canary and rolling back while we patch.
infra-bot: pausing rollout of r/4578 -> canary paused at 5%
Maria Chen: mitigation options: 1) restore threshold to 1024 2) decrease batch boundary fragmentation (force grouping by seq_len buckets) 3) force immediate slab compaction after allocation burst (cheap hack).
Zhang Wei: perf numbers: patch 1 (restore threshold) drops tail latency back to baseline, memory fragmentation reduces ~70% in repeated runs. Patch 3 helps but adds CPU jitter.
Samir Patel: preparing PR to revert threshold change + add a regression test for long mixed-seq workloads. cc @Devon O'Neill for review.
Devon O'Neill: also adding a KV compaction telemetry check to CI so we catch future regressions: `ci/bench_longctx.sh` will fail if fragmented_pages > 25%
Maria Chen: ok let's block the merge until revert lands. Create a follow-up issue with root-cause steps and assign to runtime.
ops: created INC-2026-045 (Rollout blocked: KV OOMs after kernel-router change).
infra-bot: rollback PR submitted: r/4578-revert-threshold (draft).
Samir Patel: will monitor canary and CI after revert lands. Thanks all :heart:
Maria Chen: great triage. Follow-ups: add unit/regression test, add CI fragment check, and investigate long-term fix for allocator compaction heuristics.
